analysis:
The only change in this PR is a documentation addition to docs/developer/test.md, head lines 729-746 (patch hunk @@ -726,6 +726,24). It describes the PR-reviewer tooling tests: workload fixture segmentation, removal of duplicate Opus passes, routing regressions, retained independent depth for production AppAttest.swift, Attest.swift and AuthLatest.swift, global uncertainty denying clearance, a 500-request cap, client timeout configuration, stage-admission failure attribution, manual job reruns doing no paid work, and final incomplete outcomes requiring human review. This is test-guide prose with no executable code, workflow, protocol, key handling, attestation logic, cache storage or authorization behavior changed.

I checked the text against the threat model. It does not touch the coordinator-to-provider WebSocket contract (TB-002), the operator/process boundary (TB-003), the inference engine (TB-007), the attestation chain (TB-009), the fan helper (TB-010) or App Attest authorization (TB-011). It also leaves the T-041 prefix-cache posture untouched: TTL, HMAC lookup tags, kill switch and SEC-035 are unchanged. The base-side units (:3, :4) show unchanged surrounding documentation, including the provider endpoint-resumption and logout tests, the native serving qualification and the SSD test guidance. None of that is altered.

The added text states that the review tooling keeps a fail-closed posture: it denies clearance on uncertainty, requires human review for incomplete outcomes, and restricts manual dispatch to unpaid preflight. That is consistent with the existing security posture and weakens no control. The claim that dropping duplicate Opus passes loses no source coverage is a claim about tooling code outside the supplied evidence, which I could not verify. The risk is low and documentation-only, but the actual scanner and workflow changes, if any exist in other batches, should get their own review. No findings.
